# Documentation

MkDocs site using Material theme with slate color scheme.

## Building Docs

```bash
# Generate docs from proto definitions (from repo root)
./generate_docs.sh

# Local preview
uv run mkdocs serve
```

Dependencies: `uv sync --group docs`

## Generated Content - DO NOT EDIT

These are regenerated by `./generate_docs.sh`:
- `subjects-and-types.md`
- `qos-profiles.md`
- `interfaces.md`
- `payloads/` (all files)
- `interfaces/` (all files within docs/)
- `protocols/` (all files, including `index.md` and the literate-nav `SUMMARY.md`)

Generation scripts:
- `scripts/generate_docs_for_subjects_and_types.py` — reads `messages/subjects.yaml` + `messages/payloads/`
- `scripts/generate_docs_for_qos.py` — reads `messages/qos.yaml`
- `scripts/generate_docs_for_interfaces.py` — reads `interfaces/`
- `scripts/generate_docs_for_protocols.py` — reads `protocols/*.yaml`; validates before rendering, so it fails rather than emit a page the tests would reject

`scripts/commented_yaml.py` is what lets the first two carry the YAML files'
**comments** onto the page. Roughly half of `subjects.yaml` and `qos.yaml` is
comment, and that half is the only place the units, the `source_id`
conventions, the provenance and the deliberate omissions are written down —
`yaml.safe_load` drops all of it (keelson#87). Two conventions matter when
editing those files:

- A comment line wrapped in `### ... ###` (subjects.yaml) or `# --- ... ---`
  (qos.yaml) becomes an `##` heading. Everything else becomes prose, placed
  above the subjects it precedes in the file.
- A line indented by two or more spaces inside a comment block is fenced rather
  than reflowed, so key-expression examples keep their alignment.

`sdks/python/tests/test_commented_yaml.py` fails if a comment stops reaching the
page, or if the scanner and `yaml.safe_load` ever disagree about the keys.

## Hand-Written Pages (Safe to Edit)

- `index.md` — home page
- `protocol-specification.md` — protocol spec
- `health-monitoring.md` — health monitoring guide
- `how-to-use.md` — usage guide
- `existing-resources.md` — links to related projects

## mkdocs.yml

Located at repo root (`/mkdocs.yml`), not in `docs/`. Key settings:
- Theme: Material, slate scheme, `custom_dir: overrides`
- Navigation: listed in `nav:`, except the Protocols section, whose sidebar
  literate-nav reads from the generated `docs/protocols/SUMMARY.md`
- Extensions: attr_list, md_in_html, superfences, tabbed
- Custom JS/CSS: glightbox for image lightboxes (in `docs/assets/`)
- `plugins.mike` with `canonical_version: latest`, and `extra.version` — the
  version switcher (see Release)

## Release

The published site is **versioned with mike**. Every stable release deploys a
whole copy of the site to the `gh-pages` branch under `/<major>.<minor>/` and
moves the `latest` alias onto it; `/keelson/` redirects to `latest`, and the
header carries a switcher built at runtime from `versions.json`. Nothing but a
stable release deploys.

- `uv run mkdocs serve` previews the current tree, unversioned — this is what
  you want while writing.
- `uv run mike serve` serves what is actually on `gh-pages`, all versions and
  the switcher. `uv run mike list` prints them.
- Requires protodot + graphviz for proto diagrams.
- `mike deploy` shells out to a bare `mkdocs build` and **cannot be given
  `--strict`**, so CI and the release job each run their own strict build as a
  gate. A published version is never rebuilt, so a dead link would be permanent.
- `overrides/main.html` fills Material's `outdated` block, which is empty by
  default — without it `extra.version.default` would show nothing.
- `.github/pages/404.html` is copied to the `gh-pages` root on each deploy. It
  sends pre-versioning URLs (`/keelson/subjects-and-types/`) to the same page
  under `latest/`.
